geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant bar into a gently bent bar to strengthen the continuous gesture and improve access-edge response without losing the single-mass reading.
Keep the bend modest so the mass remains coherent and capacity-aware rather than becoming a fragmented sculptural form.
Increase void size slightly to make the court legible in plan and section.
Open the courtyard toward the access side to reinforce the public threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Introduce a gentle bend into the dominant bar so the mass better acknowledges the frontage and gains a more sectional, less box-like silhouette while preserving the primary gesture.
Slightly enlarge the carved court so the void reads as a more meaningful public threshold and not just an internal subtraction.
Align the carved void to the verified access side so the ground response is semantically consistent with the street edge.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent single bar with a carved central void, and it is legible across all four views. The parcel relationship is acceptable: the mass stays within the green boundary rather than merely filling the box, and the long-bar orientation is not obviously contradictory to the site figure. The blue frontage edge is answered weakly but present through the open ground/void logic rather than a fully sealed edge. It is not a great public-edge resolution, but it is coherent enough for an early massing diagram. The section is calm and capacity-aware, with a courtyard-like subtraction that supports the neighborhood-living brief better than a purely sculptural object. No visible view-to-view collision issues appear, and the form has a clear dominant mass with one main void rather than fragmented pieces.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this low bar candidate; use only the clarity of mass-void hierarchy, not the vertical typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mass with a carved/offset upper condition can stay legible while still reading as a single civic-commercial object.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Typologically off for neighborhood living here; the candidate should not drift toward a tower interpretation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A slender, slightly deforming vertical profile can express a strong dominant gesture without losing coherence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is much lower and more street-object oriented; do not copy its literal canopy/sign language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A calmer primary volume with a distinct ground-edge response and a smaller attached marker can support neighborhood retail/public life.

warnings: Public frontage response is modest; the access edge could be articulated more explicitly in a later pass.
The mass is still somewhat generic/box-derived, so stronger section profiling could improve program specificity.
Reference 2 is only weakly relevant and should not steer the design toward a tower typology.
